issue.title: test_timeout_leaves_enough_reserve_for_cleanup ran its full 30s blocked render once under a loaded full lane
issue.description:
Proposed by the sase-1tz land agent from the epic's DISCOVERED ISSUE note #1 item (3)
(recorded by sase-1uj.land on 2026-11-20; evidence artifact
file:explicit:da2691fcb96155711373b1f0). The node was introduced by epic commit
c756511c11 (sase-1tz.2.1.4, "reserve 15s for publisher drain cleanup") and moved
unchanged into tests/agents_sync/test_commit_publication_bounded_drain_budget.py by the
1d821e0c95 test split.

## Observations

- FAIL once: phase ToolRun 0969175d22c2ec238390416539271827 (loaded full lane,
  2026-11-20) recorded FLAKY with 33.38 s duration. The retained phase log was truncated
  before the traceback, so the failing assertion is unknown.
- PASS: exact isolated rerun on clean master 7e590921e3 (1 passed in 5.83 s, call
  2.33 s, by sase-1uj.land); the full-suite escalations d3adc7ab6cd66e963ccabbaf4b676910
  and e09f2dea (phase sase-1tz.4.1.5) passed on the same family of trees; the sase-1tz
  land agent's rerun of the whole module on 39b594a30c passed this node in 2.32 s call.
- Fail rate so far: 1 failure / many passes; serial reproduction not observed.

## Mechanism hypothesis

The test drives a 30 s blocked render that the SIGALRM drain work-alarm (1.0 s) must
unwind, then asserts cleanup telemetry (`cleanup_seconds >= 1.0` and `< 2.5`) and a
queued, unpublished outcome. The 33.38 s duration ≈ 30 s sleep + setup + cleanup, which
suggests the drain alarm did not interrupt the render at all in the failing run (not a
mere tolerance overrun). That matches the load-sensitive SIGALRM bounded-drain family
tracked by sase-xo (swallowed/undelivered alarms, cleanup-budget overruns under host
load), but the node differs and the missing traceback prevents claiming an identical
root cause, so this is a node-specific task per the retired-umbrella/node-task
convention.

## Fix direction

When it recurs with a traceback, determine which assertion failed. If the render ran its
full 30 s, investigate ITIMER_REAL/SIGALRM interference in the worker process
(process-global timer state is the sase-j7 theme) rather than widening the 2.5 s
tolerance, which would not have saved the observed failure.
